pages.observation: How I read it: P1 (top left): 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' Raman and Meera are shown silent. P2 (top right): 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' with Priya. P3 (middle left): 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' with Ravi. P4 (middle right): 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' No faces, presumably a phone insert. P5 (bottom): 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.', then the teal label 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' at top-right. Raman, Priya and Ravi stand in a row from left to right below it. Issues: (1) The 'A later morning' time jump is clearly marked. (2) The page is all narration with no voices, so it reads like a slideshow. That may be intended, but think about adding one short line or reaction. (3) The text never names Raman or Priya. The reader cannot tell whether Priya in P2 is at home or already at the clinic, so the art must show where she is. (4) 'patients can always check in' is awkward. 'can still check in' or 'can check in' may read better. (5) P5 implies Raman, Priya and Ravi map to A-10, A-11 and A-12 by their left-to-right order. That works only if the art keeps that order, because page 4 relies on Ravi being A-12. (6) The gutters in the middle row do not line up with the top row. This is cosmetic and does not cause a reading problem. Nothing covers a face.
